Question: Which magazine produces more print editions yearly, Nautilus or TV Guide?
Thought 1: I need to find out how many print editions each magazine, Nautilus and TV Guide, produces yearly, and then compare them.
Action 1: Search[Nautilus (magazine)]
Observation 1: Could not find Nautilus (magazine). Similar: ['Nautilus Quarterly', 'The Nautilus (magazine)', 'Nautilus (genus)', 'Nautilus (TV series)', 'Nautilus'].
Thought 2: I should search for "The Nautilus (magazine)" since "Nautilus (magazine)" was not found, and it is a similar entity.
Action 2: Search[The Nautilus (magazine)]
Observation 2: The Nautilus was a magazine of the New Thought Movement, founded in 1898 by Elizabeth Towne, in Portland, Oregon.. The magazine was briefly published in Sioux Falls, South Dakota in 1899; however, in May 1900, Towne moved to Holyoke, Massachusetts,[1] which became the magazine's permanent home until its discontinuation in August 1953, when Towne retired from publishing at the age of 88. Towne also published, under the "Elizabeth Towne" imprint, books consisting of material which had run in serialized form in the magazine, generally supplying introductions to the compiled works.. Authors who were published in the magazine include:. In 1907, writer Grace MacGowan Cooke contributed to The Nautilus.
Thought 3: This article is about "The Nautilus" magazine, which was discontinued in 1953. The question asks about current print editions, so this is not the correct magazine. I need to find "Nautilus" magazine. I will try a more general search.
Action 3: Search[Nautilus magazine]
Observation 3: Nautilus is an American popular science magazine featuring journalism, essays, graphic narratives, fiction, and criticism. It covers most areas of science, and related topics in philosophy, technology, and history. Nautilus is published six times annually, with some of the print issues focusing on a selected theme, which also appear on its website. Issue themes have included human uniqueness, time, uncertainty, genius, mergers & acquisitions, creativity, consciousness, and reality, among many others.[1]. In Nautilus' launch year (2013), it was cited as one of Library Journal's Ten Best New Magazines Launched;[2] was named one of the World's Best-Designed news sites by the Society for News Design;[3] received an honorary mention as one of RealClearScience's top science news sites;[4] and received three awards from FOLIO: magazine, including Best Consumer Website and Best Full Issue.[5].
Thought 4: Nautilus magazine is published six times annually. Now I need to find out how many print editions TV Guide produces yearly.
Action 4: Search[TV Guide]
Observation 4: TV Guide is an American digital media company that provides television program listings information as well as entertainment and television-related news.[2][3]. In 2008, the company sold its founding product, the TV Guide magazine and the entire print magazine division, to a private buyout firm operated by Andrew Nikou, who then set up the print operation as TV Guide Magazine LLC.[4]. The prototype of what would become TV Guide magazine was developed by Lee Wagner (1910–1993),[5] who was the circulation director of MacFadden Publications in New York City in the 1930s – and later, by the time of the predecessor publication's creation, for Cowles Media Company – distributing magazines focusing on movie celebrities.[6]. In 1948, Wagner printed New York City area listings magazine The TeleVision Guide, which was first released on local newsstands on June 14 of that year. Silent film star Gloria Swanson, who then starred in the short-lived variety series The Gloria Swanson Hour, appeared on the cover of the first issue.
Thought 5: The article mentions that in 2008, the print magazine division of TV Guide was sold to a private buyout firm, but it doesn't specify how many print editions are published yearly. I need to find information about the current publication frequency of TV Guide magazine.
Action 5: Search[TV Guide magazine publication frequency]
Observation 5: Could not find TV Guide magazine publication frequency. Similar: ['TV Guide (magazine)', 'TV Guide (Canada)', 'Michelin Guide', 'Triangle Publications', 'TVTimes (redirect from Tv times)'].
Thought 6: I will search for "TV Guide (magazine)" to find more specific information about its publication frequency.
Action 6: Search[TV Guide (magazine)]
Observation 6: TV Guide is an American biweekly magazine that provides television program listings information as well as television-related news, celebrity interviews and gossip, film reviews, crossword puzzles, and, in some issues, horoscopes. The print magazine's operating company, TV Guide Magazine LLC, is owned by NTVB Media since 2015.[3] The magazine was spun off from TV Guide in 2008 by then-owner Macrovision to OpenGate Capital for $1 and a $9.5 million loan.[3]. TV Guide Magazine has a license to use the TV Guide name and distinctive red and white logo in print publications only; it is prohibited from using the branding or logo online.[3]  While the TV Guide trademark and other intellectual property is owned by Fandom, Inc., the TV Guide name and editorial content from the magazine are licensed by Fandom for use on the magazine's promotional website and mobile app.[4][5]. The prototype of what would become TV Guide magazine was developed by Lee Wagner (1910–1993),[6] who was the circulation director of MacFadden Publications in New York City in the 1930s – and later, by the time of the predecessor publication's creation, for Cowles Media Company – distributing magazines focusing on movie celebrities.. In 1948, he printed New York City area listings magazine The TeleVision Guide, which was first released on local newsstands on June 14 of that year.
Thought 7: TV Guide is a biweekly magazine. This means it is published every two weeks. There are 52 weeks in a year, so a biweekly magazine would produce 52/2 = 26 print editions yearly. Nautilus is published six times annually. Since 26 (TV Guide) > 6 (Nautilus), TV Guide produces more print editions yearly.
Action 7: Finish[TV Guide]
